# **Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology (SLIIT): Institutional and Undergraduate Programme Audit**

## **1\. Institution Overview**

### **Institutional Identity, Origins, and Scale**

The Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology (SLIIT) operates as Sri Lanka’s largest non-state tertiary education institution via its primary official portal at https\://www\.sliit.lk/about1. Founded in 1999 at the BOC Merchant Tower in Colombo to address a severe national shortage of information technology specialists, the institution welcomed its inaugural intake of 400 students in 2000 (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history)1. By 2001, SLIIT officially attained status as a degree-awarding institute and surpassed 1,000 annual student enrollments by 2002 (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history)1. Over a 25-year operational trajectory culminating in its Silver Jubilee celebrations in 2025, SLIIT expanded beyond computing into a multi-disciplinary higher education system serving over 25,000 active students across more than 100 local and transnational degree programmes, achieving a stated 98% graduate employability rate and ranking joint 3rd in Sri Lanka in the 2026 Times Higher Education World University Ranking (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about, https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bba-hons-specialising-in-accounting-finance)1.  
An examination of the institution's historical milestone sequence (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history) demonstrates a deliberate two-stage institutional evolution1. During its first decade (1999–2008), SLIIT relied on transnational articulations—beginning with external university affiliations in 2003 and the delivery of British degrees in partnership with Sheffield Hallam University (SHU) in 2004 for IT and 2008 for Electronic Engineering—to establish academic credibility and instructional capacity (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history)1. During its second decade (2011–2021), SLIIT institutionalized autonomous local faculties, establishing the SLIIT Faculty of Business (SBS) in 2011, the Faculty of Engineering in 2012, Tourism and Hospitality Management with William Angliss in 2013, the School of Architecture in 2016, the Faculty of Humanities and Sciences in 2018, the SLIIT School of Law in 2019, and the BSc (Hons) in Financial Mathematics and Applied Statistics in 2021, while becoming the first Sri Lankan campus to transition fully to online and hybrid instruction during the 2020 pandemic (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history)1. These academic expansions were accompanied by professional accreditations from the Engineering Council UK and the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET) in 2015, alongside full accreditation from Engineers Australia (EA) for Curtin University engineering programmes in 2017 (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/history)1.

### **Legal Status, Governance, and Regulatory Recognition**

While SLIIT identifies itself as "Sri Lanka’s largest non-state tertiary education provider" on https\://www\.sliit.lk/about, specific corporate registration numbers, statutory acts, or enabling gazette citations are **Not found** on its institutional governance page (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/governance)1. Cross-referencing with the official University Grants Commission (UGC) of Sri Lanka portal (https\://eugc.ugc.ac.lk/ugc\_payment/index.php/forms/form\_recognition) confirms that SLIIT is classified by the national regulator under the statutory category of *"Recognition of degrees of Non-state Institutes as published by Gazette notifications"* alongside the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU) and the University of Vocational Technology3. Furthermore, SLIIT academics serve directly on UGC Quality Assurance Council (QAC) Subject Benchmark Statement panels for Information Technology (https\://eugc.ugc.ac.lk/qac/downloads/SB/SBS-IT.pdf) and external Programme Review manual drafting committees (https\://eugc.ugc.ac.lk/qac/downloads/PR-manual-final-1-Version-3-amended-28-Dec-2015-3.pdf), confirming regulatory integration within Levels 5 and 6 of the Sri Lanka Qualification Framework (SLQF)4.  
Institutional governance (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/governance, https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/leadership) is structured around four operational pillars—Risk, Compliance & Audit; Academic Integrity; Research Standards; and University Structure—overseen by a dual corporate-academic hierarchy1. Executive leadership is headed by Prof. Lakshman Ratnayake as Chancellor and Chairman (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about) and Prof. Lalith Gamage as Vice-Chancellor, Managing Director, and CEO (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about), supported by the Board of Directors, the Council ("Our Council"), Senior Management, Senate Members, and University Management (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/leadership)1. Individual roster names for the Board of Directors, Council, and Senate are **Not found** on https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/leadership1. At the institutional level (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/accreditation-affiliation-and-awards, https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-computing), SLIIT documents three overarching approvals and memberships: approval and recognition from the Ministry of Education and University Grants Commission (*"UGC\|MOE. Recognition/Approvals by the national regulatory body, ensuring the institution adheres to educational standards set by the government of Sri Lanka"*), membership in the International Association of Universities (*"A global network of higher education institutions, ensuring SLIIT's alignment with global education standards"*), and membership in the Association of Commonwealth Universities (*"A membership highlighting SLIIT's global presence and networking within Commonwealth institutions"*) (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-computing)1.

### **Academic Structure and Campus Network**

SLIIT organizes its academic offerings across seven faculties and schools (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program)7. The **Faculty of Computing** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-computing) encompasses the Departments of Computer Science, Computer Systems Engineering, Information Technology, and Software Engineering6. The **Faculty of Engineering** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-engineering) comprises the Departments of Civil Engineering, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Quantity Surveying7. The **SLIIT Business School** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/sliit-business-school) houses the Departments of Business Management and Information Management7. The **Faculty of Humanities & Sciences** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-humanities-sciences) oversees Applied Sciences, Linguistics, Mathematics and Statistics, the School of Education, the School of Law, the School of Nursing, and the School of Psychology7. These four core faculties are complemented by the **School of Architecture** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/school-of-architecture), the **School of Business and AI** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/school-of-business-and-ai), and the **Faculty of Graduate Studies & Research** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-graduate-studies-research), the latter of which is excluded from this undergraduate and pre-university audit7.  
Instruction is delivered across seven geographic campuses and regional centers (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/campus-and-centers, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program), supplemented by four local affiliated institutions listed as CAHM, ALTHIA, SLIIT CONNECT, and SCU (https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/campus-and-centers)1.

### **Institutional Fee Architecture, Scholarships, and Funding Mechanisms**

SLIIT operates a tiered tuition pricing model (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs, https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-students/fees) that segments students by residency status (Domestic vs. International), academic discipline, and awarding body12. Domestic students are defined as *"Citizens or permanent residents of Sri Lanka (including those who completed schooling under the local curriculum such as GCE A/L or London curriculum or equivalent)"*, whereas international students are defined as *"anyone who is not a citizen or permanent resident of Sri Lanka"* and are subject to USD-denominated fees plus a *"Transnational Educational Fee: Applicable only to foreign degrees completed at SLIIT"* (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs, https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-students/fees)12. Because SLIIT does not publish a consolidated domestic fee schedule on its general fees page (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs), aggregating the verified fee structures across individual programme pages reveals a 6.1-fold price dispersion across domestic undergraduate tracks.

This fee distribution reflects a deliberate market-positioning and cross-subsidization architecture. Bachelor of Education (Hons) degrees in the Faculty of Humanities & Sciences are priced at LKR 100,000 per semester (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bed-hons-in-english, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bed-hons-in-social-sciences), enabling SLIIT to attract prospective secondary school educators at a fraction of standard private university tuition13. Core four-year Honours degrees in the Faculty of Computing are priced at LKR 375,000 per semester for the first three semesters and LKR 385,000 per semester for the final five semesters, totaling LKR 3,050,000 (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs\#payment-to-sliit)22. Local four-year Engineering Honours degrees carry a 22.6% premium over initial computing rates at LKR 460,000 per semester (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-engineering-hons-in-civil-engineering), reflecting physical laboratory capital intensity, while the University of Queensland (UQ) 2+2 Electrical Engineering pathway charges LKR 610,000 per semester during the local SLIIT phase (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-engineering-hons-electrical-electrical)23.  
To support student liquidity across these price tiers, SLIIT documents 11 scholarship and government funding schemes (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/scholarships, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/assistance, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/bank-loans)12. Under public funding, SLIIT participates in the **Ministry of Education Interest-Free Student Loan Scheme (IFSLS)** (*"The Sri Lankan Ministry of Education offers an Interest-Free Student Loan Scheme for eligible students enrolling in selected degree programmes at approved institutions, including SLIIT"*, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/bank-loans, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/government-loan-schemes)12. For incoming high achievers, SLIIT offers the **Nena Diriya Future Leaders Scholarship** (full tuition waiver plus monthly stipend for students achieving the highest national GCE A/L results in their discipline), **SLIIT Scholarships for Outstanding Performance in A/L Examination** (competitive annual merit awards for 3 As in local GCE A/L or 3 A*s / 4 A*s in one sitting of Cambridge/Edexcel A/L), and **Scholarships for Island Rankers** (full scholarships for 1st, 2nd, or 3rd island ranks across Engineering Technology, Bio Systems Technology, Arts, and Commerce streams) (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/scholarships)12.  
Continuing and specialized students have access to **SLIIT Scholarships for Semester-Based Academic Performance** (full or partial tuition waivers for students ranking in the top 1%–2% of their degree programme each semester), **School-Based and Academic-Tenure Sports & Extra-Curricular Scholarships** (recognizing provincial, national, or international achievement), **Industry Partner-Based Scholarships** (including IFS merit scholarships offered since 2004, LOLC Scholarships, MillenniumIT ESP Scholarships, and the HCL TechBee Early Career Program), the **Lalith Athulathmudali Foundation (LAF) Scholarship** (partial tuition fee waivers), the **Ananda College Old Boys' Association (ACOBA) Discount** (a 10% concession on the first-year local tuition fee component offered since 2022), **Need-Based & Charity / Individual Donor Scholarships**, and internal **HELP Loans, Bursaries, and Monthly Installment Plans** administered through the Enrolment Division for prospective students and the Student Services Division for current students (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/scholarships, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/assistance)12. Furthermore, SLIIT facilitates commercial educational loans (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/bank-loans) with **Bank of Ceylon** (applicant bears minimum 20% of course fee; maximum duration of course \+ 4 years with grace period equal to course duration; requires two guarantors up to Rs. 1.0 Mn and immovable property mortgage above Rs. 1.0 Mn; interest at Monthly AWPLR \+ 3.0% p.a. with a 22% floor up to 5 years, or Monthly AWPLR \+ 3.5% p.a. with a 24% floor up to 7 years), **Hatton National Bank** (covers up to 90% of course fee; no security required up to Rs. 5 Mn; repayment up to 12 years including up to 5-year grace period), and **Sampath Bank** (up to Rs. 10.0 Mn; repayment up to 8 years with up to 3-year grace period; 50% processing fee discount)12.

### **Standard Payment, Application, and Refund Terms**

Across all undergraduate and foundation programmes, applications are processed via the central admissions portal https\://apply.sliit.lk/ following a five-step online workflow: submitting initial details, verifying email via OTP, completing the online application form, paying the application fee, and submitting the application28. All applicants must pay a non-refundable Aptitude Test application fee as stated on https\://apply.sliit.lk/: \*"Applicants are expected to pay \*Rs. 2, 000/- as the application fee for the Aptitude Test, in favour of 'Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology' to any one of the following bank accounts... *Please note that foreign nationals are subject to an international student application fee"*28. While the General Aptitude Test is held online, the BSc (Hons) Computer Science requires a physical Special Aptitude Test on campus at Malabe, and the BSc (Hons) Architecture and BA (Hons) Interior Design programmes require a physical special drawing test at Malabe (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/new-students)9.  
Tuition and application payments can be executed online via Visa or Mastercard at https\://pay.sliit.lk or deposited at any branch of **Bank of Ceylon** (Account No. 1630552 / 0001630552, Kollupitiya Super Grade Branch), **Sampath Bank** (Account No. 00 399 0000033 / 003990000033, Malabe Branch), or **Hatton National Bank** (Account No. 156010007350, Malabe Branch) (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/new-students, https\://apply.sliit.lk/)9. SLIIT enforces a strict institutional refund policy across its domestic foundation and international student schedules: *"Fees paid are normally non-refundable. Refund requests may be considered if submitted within one week from the start date of lectures for the respective semester (for new applicants, this is counted from the start date of the Orientation Programme lectures). If approved, refunds are subject to a 10% deduction of the fee paid"* (https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-students/fees, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/sliit-international-foundation)12.

While the main search filter on https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program displays aggregate schedule counts (*"Weekdays 36, Weekends 7, Weekdays/Weekends 166"*) that combine postgraduate degrees, campus-specific permutations, and foreign partner pathways (https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-degrees/curtin-university, https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-degrees/ljmu-university, https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-degrees/deakin-university, https\://www\.sliit.lk/international-degrees/manchester-metropolitan-university, https\://www\.sliit.lk/global-pathways/university-of-queensland, https\://www\.sliit.lk/global-pathways/university-of-edinburgh, https\://www\.sliit.lk/global-pathways/university-of-western-australia), the inventory below catalogues every individual undergraduate degree, foundation course, higher diploma, and professional diploma directory discovered across official SLIIT URLs7.

## **3\. Programme-by-Programme Fact Sheets**

This section documents comprehensive, evidence-backed fact sheets for **24 programmes**, representing **100% coverage of the undergraduate degree portfolio of the Faculty of Computing** (12 degree programmes plus the IT Bridging track), the **SLIIT International Foundation (SIF)** programme, and **11 additional undergraduate degree programmes** across the Faculty of Engineering (6), SLIIT Business School (3), and Faculty of Humanities & Sciences (2). Each fact sheet pairs a structured parameter table with supporting documentary context and verbatim excerpts.

### **Subsection A: Pre-University Foundation Programmes**

#### **Fact Sheet \#1: SLIIT International Foundation (SIF)**

The SLIIT International Foundation (SIF) serves as the institution's primary pre-university bridge for students completing Ordinary Level qualifications who seek direct entry into transnational partner degrees delivered at SLIIT or overseas (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/sliit-international-foundation)15. Critically, the programme's official FAQ clarifies a regulatory boundary: GCE Advanced Level (A/L) passes remain mandatory for admission into local SLIIT-awarded degrees, meaning the SIF pathway is restricted to progressing into foreign partner university degrees (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/sliit-international-foundation)15.

| **Teaching & Awarding Body** | Taught and awarded by **SLIIT** (Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology) (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/sliit-international-foundation)15 |

#### **Fact Sheet \#4: BSc (Hons) in Information Technology Specializing in Information Technology (and IT Bridging Programme)**

This flagship SLQF Level 06 degree provides comprehensive training in software engineering, operating systems, database systems, cloud computing, and enterprise IT governance (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-information-technology-specializing-in-information-technology)11. Notably, its detail page documents the exact mechanics of SLIIT's **IT Bridging Programme**, which allows students from non-Physical Science/Engineering Technology A/L streams to enter computing degrees provided they hold a 'C' pass in O/L Mathematics (with an exemption granted to students who passed ICT or Computer Science as a main A/L subject) (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-information-technology-specializing-in-information-technology)11.

## **5\. Missing Information and Conflicting Claims**

### **Conflicting Official Claims**

A cross-document verification of SLIIT’s official web pages and downloadable PDF guides reveals five substantive contradictions across published materials. The most financially significant conflict involves a four-way discrepancy in domestic tuition fees for the Faculty of Computing’s four-year BSc (Hons) degrees. First, the downloadable **2025 Student Guide PDF** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/download/study/sliit-student-guide-2025-v1.pdf) states: *"The fee is Rs. 340,000 per semester till year 2 semester 1 and Rs. 350,000"* per semester thereafter, yielding an 8-semester cumulative cost of LKR 2,770,00057. Second, the downloadable **2026 Student Guide PDF** (https\://webasset.sliit.lk/web/sliit-student-guide-2026-v1\_1770438399.pdf) states: *"The fee is Rs. 350,000 per semester till year 2 semester 1 and Rs. 360,000"* per semester thereafter, yielding an 8-semester cumulative cost of LKR 2,850,00056. Third, the live **2026/2027 Intake web pages** for Software Engineering, Data Science, Cyber Security, Computer Systems & Network Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and Creative Computing (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-software-engineering, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs\#payment-to-sliit) state: *"Fees per semester are LKR 375,000 for the first year, and the first semester of year 2\. For each subsequent semester, the fee is LKR 385,000"*, yielding an 8-semester cumulative cost of LKR 3,050,00010. Fourth, the live web page for **BSc (Hons) in Information Technology Specializing in Information Technology** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-information-technology-specializing-in-information-technology) states a flat *"Semester Fee: LKR 375,000 per semester"* without mentioning the LKR 385,000 step-up from Year 2 Semester 2 onward, which would equal LKR 3,000,000 over eight semesters11. This progression indicates a 2.9% tuition revision between the 2025 and 2026 PDF guides followed by a 7.1% upward revision for the 2026/2027 intake web pages, while older PDF prospectuses remain simultaneously hosted on SLIIT servers.  
![][image1]  
Four additional official contradictions appear across specific programme and faculty pages. First, on both the **Bachelor of Computer Science** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-computer-science) and **Bachelor of Commerce** (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-commerce) pages for the University of Queensland pathway, the main Entry Requirements section states *"The Applicant should maintain minimum GPA of 2.5 to transfer"*, whereas the FAQ section on the exact same pages states *"Yes, students should maintain 2.7 GPA when transferring to the UQ"*31. Second, on the **BSc Engineering (Hons) in Materials Engineering** page (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-engineering-hons-in-materials-engineering), while the overview and module table (MT2050 Ceramics Engineering, Chemical Thermodynamics & Phase Equilibria) accurately describe Materials Engineering, the Year 1–4 Programme Structure prose block erroneously reproduces the **Mechatronics Engineering** curriculum (*"Second Year. Specialization begins with courses in digital design, embedded systems, and mechatronics project development... Third Year. Advanced mechatronic systems, control systems, automation, and robotics... Fourth Year. Research and design projects and electives in artificial intelligence, machine vision, industrial automation, and micro-mechatronics"*)33. Third, on https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-business-management, the page heading reads *"Bachelor Of Business Management"*, but the opening sentence of its overview describes it as *"The BBA (Hons) in Business Administration develops leadership, innovation, and adaptability skills..."* while attributing the award to the University of Queensland37. Fourth, on the Faculty of Computing directory pages (https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-computing/study and https\://www\.sliit.lk/academic/faculty-of-computing), "Computer Science" and "Information Technology" appear twice in the summary cards—once with a 3-year duration (referring to the UQ-awarded Bachelor degrees) and once with a 4-year duration (referring to the SLIIT-awarded BSc Honours degrees)—without visually distinguishing the awarding institution on the directory card6.

### **Systematic Missing Information ("Not Found")**

Several categories of institutional and programme-level data are systematically absent from SLIIT’s public web pages and marked **Not found** in this audit. At the institutional level, exact corporate incorporation numbers, statutory acts, or enabling gazette dates are **Not found** on https\://www\.sliit.lk/about or https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/governance, and the individual names of members serving on the Board of Directors, Council, and Senate are **Not found** on https\://www\.sliit.lk/about/leadership1. Similarly, the central Fees and Costs portal (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/fees-and-scholarships/fees-and-costs) and the undergraduate search directory (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program?ptype=undergraduate) omit a master domestic tuition table, requiring prospective applicants to inspect individual programme pages or contact the Enrolment Division12.  
At the individual programme level, specific A/L entry requirements are **Not found** on https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-cyber-security, its linked brochure https\://webasset.sliit.lk/web/Brochure-Cyber-Security\_1761649213.pdf, and https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-engineering-hons-in-electrical-electronic-engineering22. Furthermore, domestic semester fee figures are **Not found** in the extracted text of https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-computer-science, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-hons-in-computer-systems-engineering, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bsc-engineering-hons-in-materials-engineering, and the University of Queensland articulation pages for Computer Science, Information Technology, Commerce, and Business Management (https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-computer-science, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-information-technology, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-commerce, https\://www\.sliit.lk/study/find-a-program/bachelor-of-business-management)29.
